edition_aid.title: Aurora consurgens: un dossier aperto
edition_aid.witness_basis: Explicitly compared Rh(Zurich) and R(Roudnice); variants not conflated
edition_aid.retained_material: Public-domain manuscript inscription text only; modern article prose not republished

rows.translation: A soluble body joined to spirit; union through a threefold humidity.
First airy combustible mercurial; second watery, namely lunar vapour; third fiery, namely solar fusibility.

published_latin: Fidibus tu patulas si cancri gesseris nostri
tria tua corisando mea sibi bursa retentat
rows.leiden_note: The second Latin line appears to begin Era tua. German counterpart mentions open ears, crab and purse retaining what belongs to the addressee. No silent emendation of Zurich.

published_latin: infatuas norma contra naturam sensuum tibi quinque
rows.leiden_note: Five senses and their rule are visible in the German ending; Latin wording differs. Whole couplet syntax unresolved.

published_latin: Fistula dulce canit mihi si non crede kathoni
dum lira dulcissono carmine prodit aves
rows.translation: The flute sings sweetly; appeal to Cato; a lyre, sweet song and birds. Exact rendering of the last predicate remains qualified.

later_witness_date: 1522-1526 main hand; not a new medieval dating of the same witness
source_result: Body/spirit union through three humidity modes plus musical/fool/senses frame; no one-to-one element-to-limb key
